findings.title: Unknown Threat Actor Uses AI-Driven ARTEX to Target South Korean Finance
findings.summary_md: CrowdStrike reported a campaign against South Korean financial organizations active from late September to early October 2026 that ended in exfiltrated data. The actor was not tied to a named group and was assessed with moderate confidence to be a Chinese speaker and financially motivated. Investigators found threat actor-controlled open directories holding Claude Code session histories, ARTEX configuration files and Claude memory files. The ARTEX host at 38.244.50[.]120 used DeepSeek v4.1-flash as its main model, and the actor likely reached it through the API reseller xcai[.]pro.

findings.title: ARTEX and Friends: Enter Agentic Offensive Frameworks
findings.summary_md: Google Threat Intelligence Group and Mandiant documented incident response engagements since late August 2026 in which actors ran ARTEX, Hexstrike, CAIRN and other agentic pentesting frameworks across reconnaissance, lateral movement, database exploitation and exfiltration preparation. They describe ARTEX as six specialized sub-agents that turn natural language goals into machine commands using external LLMs, with execution in compressed bursts of roughly 2 to 25 seconds, including 27 events in 23 seconds during AWS permission probing. The post tracks one ARTEX cluster as UNC7228, overlapping with Microsoft's STORM-0940, and reports first-account-to-deep-access times around four hours and as fast as 15 minutes.

findings.title: ARTEX: Agentic Asbestos
findings.summary_md: Censys observed 1,465 hosts running an exposed ARTEX console as of November 4, 2026, about 650 of them in two identically configured hosting blocks, leaving roughly 815 distinct-looking deployments. It found 155 ARTEX hosts, 10.6 percent of the total, also running at least one other detected threat such as Vshell, Cobalt Strike or Adaptix C2, and 32 open directories exposing post-exploitation kits, stagers and implants. Scan history showed an open directory on the host from the South Korean financial campaign as early as August 18, 2026, seven weeks before CrowdStrike published its report.

findings.title: FLASH-20261113-001, Threat Overview of ARTEX Autonomous Penetration Testing Framework
findings.summary_md: The FBI's November 13, 2026 FLASH says ARTEX, an open-source LLM-driven agentic platform, has been weaponized since at least August 2026 against organizations in financial services, government, technology, defense, healthcare and other sectors. It reports intrusions that went from initial targeting to privileged access in under three hours, personal data theft affecting roughly 67,000 people in South Korea, and access to more than 2,250 downstream ConnectWise Cloud Backup tenants. Listed indicators include the ARTEX host 38.244.50[.]120, WISP nodes 199.19.95[.]66 through 199.19.95[.]68 and the reseller domain xcai[.]pro. Recommended actions include restricting Kudu/SCM and cloud administration endpoints, reviewing Entra credential additions and hunting compressed bursts of iterative activity.

findings.title: FBI warns ARTEX AI hacking tool is powering global cyberattacks
findings.summary_md: BleepingComputer reported on November 15, 2026 that the FBI had warned about ARTEX, an AI-powered framework used since at least August 2026 to automate intrusions worldwide. The article notes that more than 1,600 ARTEX consoles were publicly exposed by early November and that the original GitHub repository was removed on October 8, 2026, while forks, archived copies and ARTEX PRO kept the tool available. It also describes the October ConnectWise Cloud Backup supply-chain attack, where compromised application identities allowed access to Microsoft 365 customer environments, and a detection signature pack released by researcher MalwareMustDie.
